accepted.s: The Simon Commission was appointed by the British Government on
accepted.x: The Simon Commission was appointed on 8 November 1927 by the Conservative Government headed by Stanley Baldwin, two years ahead of schedule.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the appointment date from the later arrival and protest dates.
accepted.sec: Simon Commission - appointment, arrival, members, boycott, slogan, Lajpat Rai  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Simon Commission was appointed primarily to
o: settle the question of communal representation
frame a constitution for an independent India
review the working of the Government of India Act, 1919
implement the recommendations of the Nehru Report
accepted.x: The Commission was appointed to review the working of the Government of India Act, 1919.
accepted.tq: Identify the statutory purpose rather than the later political consequences.
accepted.sec: Simon Commission - appointment, arrival, members, boycott, slogan, Lajpat Rai  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The principal reason for the boycott of the Simon Commission by Indian political organisations was that
o: it recommended the continuation of separate electorates
it was appointed after the Nehru Report
accepted.x: The Commission was boycotted because all its members were British and it contained no Indian member.
accepted.tq: Separate the immediate cause of boycott from later constitutional disagreements.
accepted.sec: Simon Commission - appointment, arrival, members, boycott, slogan, Lajpat Rai  [APPSC]

accepted.s: At the Madras session of the Indian National Congress in December 1927, the decision regarding the Simon Commission was to
o: boycott it only at its first meeting
send an Indian delegation to assist it
boycott it at every stage and in every form
accepted.x: The Madras Congress session under M. A. Ansari resolved to boycott the Simon Commission at every stage and in every form.
accepted.tq: Recall the precise wording of an organisational resolution.
accepted.sec: Simon Commission - appointment, arrival, members, boycott, slogan, Lajpat Rai  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which of the following groups did NOT join the boycott of the Simon Commission?
1. Jinnah's faction of the Muslim League
2. Shafi's faction of the Muslim League
3. Hindu Mahasabha
4. Justice Party
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Shafi's League faction and the Justice Party did not join the boycott. Jinnah's faction and the Hindu Mahasabha participated in it.
accepted.tq: Use organisational faction differences to identify the exceptions.
accepted.sec: Simon Commission - appointment, arrival, members, boycott, slogan, Lajpat Rai  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Lala Lajpat Rai led the protest against the Simon Commission at Lahore on
accepted.x: Lala Lajpat Rai led a peaceful protest at Lahore on 30 October 1928.
accepted.tq: Link the protest date with the later date of death caused by the injuries.
accepted.sec: Simon Commission - appointment, arrival, members, boycott, slogan, Lajpat Rai  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which one of the following correctly describes the sequence of events connected with Lala Lajpat Rai's death?
1. S. P. James Scott ordered a lathi charge.
2. Lala Lajpat Rai led a protest at Lahore.
3. Lala Lajpat Rai died of his injuries.
4. Saunders was killed by Bhagat Singh's group.
Select the correct chronological order.
accepted.x: Lajpat Rai led the protest on 30 October 1928, Scott ordered the lathi charge, Rai died on 17 November 1928, and Saunders was killed in December 1928.
accepted.tq: Fix the first protest and last revenge event, then arrange the intervening events.
accepted.sec: Simon Commission - appointment, arrival, members, boycott, slogan, Lajpat Rai  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements is correct regarding the Lahore protest against the Simon Commission?
o: S. P. James Scott ordered the lathi charge, while Saunders was later killed by Bhagat Singh's group.
Bhagat Singh led the peaceful protest and later died of lathi injuries.
Lala Lajpat Rai was killed immediately at the protest by the Simon Commission members.
Saunders ordered the lathi charge and was later killed by Lajpat Rai's followers.
accepted.x: S. P. James Scott ordered the lathi charge that injured Lajpat Rai. Bhagat Singh's group later killed Saunders in December 1928 in an act of revenge.
accepted.tq: Trap the swapped person responsible for the lathi charge and the later assassination.
accepted.sec: Simon Commission - appointment, arrival, members, boycott, slogan, Lajpat Rai  [APPSC]

accepted.s: In the Madras Presidency, the protest against the Simon Commission in 1928 was led by
accepted.x: Tanguturi Prakasam led the protest in Madras in 1928.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the regional protest leader from other Andhra organisers.
accepted.sec: Simon boycott in Andhra - Prakasam, Andhra Kesari  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Tanguturi Prakasam earned the title ‘Andhra Kesari’ because he
o: drafted the Nehru Report in Andhra
bared his chest and dared the police to shoot during the Simon protest
organised the first Round Table Conference
led the boycott resolution at the Madras Congress session
accepted.x: During the Simon protest, Prakasam bared his chest and challenged the police to shoot, earning the title ‘Andhra Kesari’.
accepted.tq: Connect an honorific with the specific incident that produced it.
accepted.sec: Simon boycott in Andhra - Prakasam, Andhra Kesari  [APPSC]

accepted.s: During the Simon Commission protest in Madras, the person killed by police firing was
accepted.x: Police firing during the Madras protest killed Parthasarathi.
accepted.tq: Identify the individual associated with a specific regional incident.
accepted.sec: Simon boycott in Andhra - Prakasam, Andhra Kesari  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Who was the President of the Andhra Boycott Committee formed in connection with the Simon Commission agitation?
accepted.x: S. Satyamurthy served as President of the Andhra Boycott Committee.
accepted.tq: Separate the committee office-holder from the field protest leaders.
accepted.sec: Simon boycott in Andhra - Prakasam, Andhra Kesari  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: G. V. Unnayya Sastri — protest at Tenali and Guntur
Bulusu Sambamurti — tour of Andhra for Simon boycott
Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao — Vijayawada boycott initiative
S. Satyamurthy — led the protest at Lahore
accepted.x: S. P. James Scott, not S. Satyamurthy, was associated with the Lahore lathi charge. The other three pairs correctly describe Andhra-related activities.
accepted.tq: Find the wrong person-to-event pairing among closely related organisers.
accepted.sec: Simon boycott in Andhra - Prakasam, Andhra Kesari  [APPSC]

accepted.s: At Vijayawada, the cover sent by Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao in protest against the Simon Commission contained only the words
accepted.x: Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao sent a cover bearing only the words ‘Simon Go Back’. The Vijayawada municipality also passed a boycott resolution.
accepted.tq: Recall the distinctive wording used in a symbolic protest action.
accepted.sec: Simon boycott in Andhra - Prakasam, Andhra Kesari  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which of the following places passed municipal resolutions supporting the boycott of the Simon Commission?
1. Vijayawada
2. Tirupati
3. Kurnool
4. Eluru
5. Srikakulam
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: The municipalities of Vijayawada, Tirupati, Kurnool, Eluru and Srikakulam passed resolutions supporting the boycott.
accepted.tq: Check every item in the regional list before selecting the complete combination.
accepted.sec: Simon boycott in Andhra - Prakasam, Andhra Kesari  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Black flags were shown against the Simon Commission at
accepted.x: Black flags were shown at Guntur and Ongole. G. V. Unnayya Sastri led protests at Tenali and Guntur.
accepted.tq: Distinguish locations of black-flag demonstrations from locations of organised leadership.
accepted.sec: Simon boycott in Andhra - Prakasam, Andhra Kesari  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The challenge issued by Birkenhead in 1927, which led to the formation of the committee for the Nehru Report, was that Indians
o: could not organise a boycott of the Simon Commission
could not agree on a constitutional scheme
accepted.x: Birkenhead challenged Indians to prepare an agreed constitutional scheme, leading to the All Parties Conference and the Nehru Report committee.
accepted.tq: Identify the cause behind the formation of a constitutional committee.
accepted.sec: Nehru Report - chairman, demand, recommendations, reactions  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the committee that prepared the Nehru Report:
1. It was constituted by an All Parties Conference.
2. Dr M. A. Ansari presided over the All Parties Conference.
3. Motilal Nehru was its chairman.
4. Jawaharlal Nehru served as its secretary.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements are correct. The seven-member committee was formed by the All Parties Conference presided over by Dr M. A. Ansari, with Motilal Nehru as chairman and Jawaharlal Nehru as secretary.
accepted.tq: Verify the formation, presiding officer, chairman and secretary separately.
accepted.sec: Nehru Report - chairman, demand, recommendations, reactions  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Nehru Report was published in
accepted.x: The Nehru Report was issued in August 1928.
accepted.tq: Reject the nearby but incorrect years associated with the committee and later reactions.
accepted.sec: Nehru Report - chairman, demand, recommendations, reactions  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following was NOT a recommendation of the Nehru Report?
o: Universal adult suffrage and fundamental rights
Separate electorates as the permanent basis of representation
A federal structure with a bicameral central legislature
accepted.x: The Nehru Report recommended joint electorates with reserved seats for minorities, not separate electorates as a permanent arrangement.
accepted.tq: Use the central distinction between joint electorates and separate electorates.
accepted.sec: Nehru Report - chairman, demand, recommendations, reactions  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which one of the following combinations correctly represents recommendations of the Nehru Report?
1. End of dyarchy
2. Responsible government
3. Establishment of a Supreme Court
4. Linguistic provinces, including Andhra
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: The Nehru Report recommended ending dyarchy, establishing responsible government and a Supreme Court, and creating linguistic provinces including Andhra.
accepted.tq: Recognise the complete set of constitutional and administrative recommendations.
accepted.sec: Nehru Report - chairman, demand, recommendations, reactions  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Nehru Report recommended which arrangement for minority representation?
o: One-third separate representation for Muslims in every province
Nomination of all minority members by the Governor-General
Joint electorates with reserved seats for minorities
accepted.x: The Report proposed joint electorates with reserved seats for minorities.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the Nehru Report proposal and Jinnah's later demands.
accepted.sec: Nehru Report - chairman, demand, recommendations, reactions  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which of the following correctly describes the reaction to the Nehru Report?
1. The Muslim League rejected it.
2. Jinnah's amendments failed at the Calcutta All Parties Convention.
3. Jawaharlal Nehru and Subhas Chandra Bose demanded complete independence.
4. The Congress immediately accepted complete independence without an ultimatum.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Congress gave Britain a one-year ultimatum; complete independence was declared at Lahore in 1929 after the ultimatum expired.
accepted.tq: Identify the single false statement by distinguishing an ultimatum from its later outcome.
accepted.sec: Nehru Report - chairman, demand, recommendations, reactions  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. Partition of Bengal
B. Simon Commission
C. Nehru Report
D. Jinnah's Fourteen Points
E. Gandhi-Irwin Pact
accepted.x: The sequence is Partition of Bengal (1905), Simon Commission (1927–28), Nehru Report (1928), Fourteen Points (1929), and Gandhi-Irwin Pact (5 March 1931).
accepted.tq: Anchor the earliest and latest events, then place the closely spaced constitutional developments.
accepted.sec: Chronology  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which one of the following correctly describes the First Round Table Conference?
1. The Congress boycotted it.
2. It was held while the Civil Disobedience Movement was continuing.
3. It was followed by the Gandhi-Irwin Pact.
4. It was conducted under Prime Minister Ramsay MacDonald.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: All four statements are correct. The First Round Table Conference was held during the Civil Disobedience Movement, without Congress participation, under Ramsay MacDonald, and was followed by the Gandhi-Irwin Pact.
accepted.tq: Combine participation, political context and consequence to identify the complete description.
accepted.sec: Round Table Conferences - dates, venue, participants, Congress attendance  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following statements about the three Round Table Conferences is correct?
o: Only the Second Conference was held in London to discuss dominion status.
All three were held in Delhi under the Viceroy of India.
The conferences were convened by the Indian National Congress to draft the Nehru Report.
All three were held in London under Ramsay MacDonald to discuss the Simon Report and a federal constitution.
accepted.x: All three Round Table Conferences were held in London under British Prime Minister Ramsay MacDonald to discuss the Simon Report and a federal constitution.
accepted.tq: Use venue, convening authority and agenda together to eliminate substituted details.
accepted.sec: Round Table Conferences - dates, venue, participants, Congress attendance  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Second Round Table Conference failed mainly because of disagreement over
o: the location of the federal capital
the appointment of the Simon Commission
accepted.x: The Second Round Table Conference failed chiefly because agreement could not be reached on minority representation.
accepted.tq: Identify the central issue that caused the conference deadlock.
accepted.sec: Round Table Conferences - dates, venue, participants, Congress attendance  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which of the following statements about the Third Round Table Conference is correct?
1. It was held from 17 November to 24 December 1932.
2. The Congress boycotted it.
3. It had only 46 delegates.
4. It contributed to the plan for the Government of India Act, 1935.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: All four statements are correct. The Third Conference was held in late 1932, was boycotted by Congress, had 46 delegates and helped shape the plan for the Government of India Act, 1935.
accepted.tq: Check the date, attendance, size and constitutional outcome as a single cluster.
accepted.sec: Round Table Conferences - dates, venue, participants, Congress attendance  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: First Round Table Conference — Congress represented by Gandhi
Second Round Table Conference — Gandhi as sole INC representative
Third Round Table Conference — attended by Congress under Jawaharlal Nehru
First Round Table Conference — held after the Gandhi-Irwin Pact
accepted.x: Gandhi attended the Second Round Table Conference as the sole representative of the Indian National Congress. Congress boycotted the First and Third Conferences.
accepted.tq: Start with the sure Congress-attendance pair and eliminate reversals.
accepted.sec: Round Table Conferences - dates, venue, participants, Congress attendance  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Dr B. R. Ambedkar attended the Round Table Conferences as a representative of the
accepted.x: Ambedkar participated in the Round Table Conferences as a representative of the depressed classes.
accepted.tq: Match the prominent delegate with the social group he represented.
accepted.sec: Round Table Conferences - dates, venue, participants, Congress attendance  [APPSC]

accepted.s: After the Second Round Table Conference, Mahatma Gandhi
o: joined the Third Round Table Conference as a British delegate
resumed the Civil Disobedience Movement and was jailed in Yerwada
formed the Muslim League to negotiate minority representation
accepted the Communal Award and retired from public life
accepted.x: After the Second Conference, Gandhi resumed the Civil Disobedience Movement and was imprisoned in Yerwada. The Communal Award followed in August 1932.
accepted.tq: Link a conference outcome with its immediate political consequence.
accepted.sec: Round Table Conferences - dates, venue, participants, Congress attendance  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Butler Committee was appointed to examine the relationship between
o: the British Parliament and the Indian National Congress
the provinces and the central legislature
the Muslim League and the Hindu Mahasabha
the Indian princely states and the Paramount Power
accepted.x: The Butler Committee, appointed in 1927 under Harcourt Butler, examined relations between the Indian princely states and the Paramount Power.
accepted.tq: Identify the exact institutional relationship under examination.
accepted.sec: Butler Committee - purpose  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Butler Committee — relations of princely states with the Paramount Power
Simon Commission — review of the Government of India Act, 1919
Butler Committee — chaired by Lord Irwin
accepted.x: The Butler Committee was associated with Harcourt Butler, not Lord Irwin. Its purpose was to examine relations between princely states and the Paramount Power.
accepted.tq: Use the swapped-person trap in a commission-to-chairman pairing.
accepted.sec: Butler Committee - purpose  [other exams]

accepted.s: Under the Delhi Proposals of March 1927, Muslim leaders offered to give up separate electorates in favour of joint electorates subject to, among others, which condition?
o: Removal of all safeguards for Muslim-majority provinces
Complete separation of Bengal from India
accepted.x: The Delhi Proposals offered joint electorates in return for safeguards including one-third Muslim representation at the centre, separation of Sindh, reforms in the North-West Frontier Province and Baluchistan, and population-based representation in Punjab and Bengal.
accepted.tq: Recall the conditional nature of a constitutional compromise.
accepted.sec: All Parties and Muslim conferences, Delhi Proposals, Fourteen Points  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Which of the following was NOT a condition associated with the Delhi Proposals?
1. Separation of Sindh
2. Reforms in the North-West Frontier Province and Baluchistan
3. One-third Muslim representation at the centre
4. Abolition of joint electorates
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: The Delhi Proposals supported joint electorates subject to safeguards; they did not seek the abolition of joint electorates. The other three were associated conditions.
accepted.tq: Identify the statement that reverses the central proposal.
accepted.sec: All Parties and Muslim conferences, Delhi Proposals, Fourteen Points  [other exams]

accepted.s: The All Parties Muslim Conference held at Delhi in January 1929, under the Aga Khan,
o: drafted the Government of India Act, 1935
resolved to boycott the Simon Commission at every stage
accepted the Nehru Report without modification
accepted.x: The All Parties Muslim Conference at Delhi in January 1929, presided over by the Aga Khan, rejected the Nehru Report.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the Muslim Conference's reaction from the earlier All Parties Conference.
accepted.sec: All Parties and Muslim conferences, Delhi Proposals, Fourteen Points  [other exams]

accepted.s: Jinnah's Fourteen Points were presented in March 1929 at the
o: Indian National Congress session at Lahore
Second Round Table Conference at London
accepted.x: Jinnah presented the Fourteen Points in March 1929 at the Muslim League session in Delhi.
accepted.tq: Match a constitutional document with its organisation, venue and date.
accepted.sec: All Parties and Muslim conferences, Delhi Proposals, Fourteen Points  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Which of the following demands formed part of Jinnah's Fourteen Points?
1. Federal constitution with residuary powers vested in the provinces
2. One-third Muslim representation at the centre
3. Separate electorates
4. Safeguards for Muslim-majority provinces
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: All four were among the major demands associated with Jinnah's Fourteen Points: provincial residuary powers, one-third central representation, separate electorates and safeguards for Muslim-majority provinces.
accepted.tq: Distinguish Jinnah's demands from the joint-electorate provisions of the Nehru Report.
accepted.sec: All Parties and Muslim conferences, Delhi Proposals, Fourteen Points  [other exams]
